params.prompt:
SHOT: Straight-on e-commerce packshot, 4:5. ONE ring only, standing upright on the top face, the two clusters facing the camera across the opening, the wide flat band's full width and its squared edges clearly visible as it curves away behind, on a cream plaster cube. Camera close, a little above the cube's top face, looking down at about thirty degrees. Macro-sharp on the metal.

THE PRODUCT: IMAGE 1 is a phone photograph of the actual piece and the ONLY authority on what it is: copy its construction, its metal colour and its stone colour EXACTLY; it is a frame from the owner's video of the ring held between two fingers over a tray of other rings: take ONLY the ring held in the fingers. IMAGE 2 is another frame of the same ring, turned to show both of its ends. IMAGE 3 is here ONLY for the plinth, the camera distance, the background and the light: copy its cube and its framing exactly and ignore everything else about it.

CONSTRUCTION LOCK: AN OPEN CLUSTER RING on a WIDE, FLAT polished gold band, exactly as IMAGE 1 and IMAGE 2 show: the band is about 10 to 12mm wide, wider than its largest stone is long, flat across its face with crisp squared edges and a mirror polish, like a wide cigar band, and it does NOT close: its two squared-off ends meet on top with a narrow gap. The stones sit LOW, close to the band's flat face beside the gap, each in small gold claws. One end carries THREE clear stones in a cluster: ONE large PEAR, ONE medium ROUND beside the pear's rounded end, and ONE small ROUND tucked between them. The other end carries THREE clear stones: TWO PEARS side by side, their rounded ends together and their points turned outward, and ONE small ROUND at their outer side, with a row of tiny gold beads running along the band's cut edge beside the pears. All stones clear. Exactly SIX stones: three pears and three rounds (one medium, two small); never coloured stones, never a full pave band, never a closed band; the band is wide and flat with squared edges, never slim, never rounded like a wire, never tapered; the stones are never raised high on posts or tall blocks.

SCALE TEST: The band is about 10 to 12mm wide; the large pear about 6 x 8mm, the medium round about 5mm, the small rounds about 3mm, the two pears on the other end about 5 x 7mm; each cluster about 10 to 12mm across. The piece keeps its true small size against the cube, never enlarged.

GROUND: The cream plaster cube fills the lower half of the frame, large and close; flat faces, softly rounded corners, fine plaster grain. Warm cream seamless behind with a gentle gradient falloff, never sand, tan, beige or golden. Soft large key from camera-left, one soft shadow, plus ONE small hard specular kicker from the right, so the metal shows a bright moving highlight and a dark rolled edge on every curve, and every stone shows internal sparkle and a hard white point, never flat colour.

ABSENCE LIST: No hand, no fingers, no model, no fabric, no props, no flowers, no box. No second piece of jewellery. Metal: warm 18k gold tone, never brassy, orange or greenish. No lettering, no watermark, no logo, no tag, no size sticker anywhere in frame. The picture runs edge to edge as a crisp, clean, modern digital studio photograph, shot today on a high-resolution digital camera.
